text: Before the trial starts, I need your real times for one normal weekday. They become the starting numbers the trial is measured against.
Rough times are fine. If nobody writes a step down today, just say so.
chat.pointer: The blank timeline shows every time I need. Type them to me in one message, in any order.
chat.note: Rough times now beat perfect times never.

points.label: When the bed is ready again

prompts: Here are the times for a normal Tuesday
We don’t write down when doctors decide
Can the Discharge Manager collect these?

blocks.title: One normal day, step by step

blocks.caption: A normal weekday on the trial ward. Rough is fine. Leave a box empty if nobody records it.

items.title: Week 1: watch
items.text: Run discharge the usual way, and write down every time above.
more_points: Nothing changes on the ward yet.
The Discharge Manager, or a nurse you choose, writes down the times for each patient.
At the end of the week we have your real starting numbers.

items.title: Week 2: the new order
items.text: Start the papers, the bill and insurance on the evening round, by hand.
more_points: Doctors say who is going home on the evening round, as they already do.
Papers and the bill are started that evening, not the next morning.
The first bill goes to insurance before the night ends.
The same times are written down, so the two weeks can be compared.

items.title: Week 3: decide
items.text: Compare the two weeks, and decide what to link first.
more_points: If the wait dropped, we know how much the software can add.
If it didn’t, the times show exactly which step held it up.
